verdict.rationale: SumUp documents webhooks, but they only report a checkout status change, and you subscribe per checkout by passing a `return_url` when creating it. There is no evidence of separate authorized, captured, refunded or disputed events, or of account-level webhook registration. missing for 10: refund event notifications, dispute/chargeback event notifications, distinct authorization vs capture events, account-level webhook subscription management, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe to payment lifecycle events (authorized, captured, refunded, disputed) via webhooks to drive downstream automations

citations.quote: At this time our system only allows you to get notified about a status change for a checkout. To subscribe to an event, specify a `return_url` parameter upon checkout creation.
